reason: Conversation 2 puts safety first: it says to stop resetting the trip, keep the appliance unplugged, not open it, and get an electrician or engineer. It also says plainly that kettles are outside its scope. Conversation 1 gives a better diagnosis (likely the kettle, water ingress, bin it, the RCD is doing its job), but it tells the customer to keep running the kettle on other sockets 'a few times' and alongside other appliances. That is unsafe with a probable earth leak and water in the base, and it only says to stop using the kettle as a conditional afterthought. Conversation 2 is thin, never says the kettle is the likely culprit, and wrongly points to manufacturer troubleshooting guides. Even so, its safety stance is closer to the expected response.
